# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lee_2026_triapine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lee_2026_triapine"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00280-026-04898-6> (open access, PMC13190473)
* Supplement: Electronic supplementary material 1 of the article (Figures S1-S3,
  Tables S1-S2, and the Pumas code of the PK model (Methods S1) and the PD model
  (Methods S2)).

Triapine (3-aminopyridine-2-carboxaldehyde thiosemicarbazone) is an oral and
intravenous ribonucleotide reductase inhibitor developed as a radiosensitizer.
Its dose-limiting toxicity is methemoglobinemia. Lee et al. fitted a sequential
population PK/PD model in Pumas: a two-compartment PK model with a
two-transit-compartment Erlang absorption chain, then an effect-compartment
sigmoid Emax model of blood methemoglobin (mHb, % of total hemoglobin) driven by
the individual PK predictions. The packaged model joins the two layers in one
`rxode2` model with two endpoints, `Cc` (plasma triapine, ug/L) and `methb`
(mHb, %).

# Population

The model was developed from 36 adults in two phase I trials (Table 1 of the
paper). NCT02595879 (NCI 9892, n = 20) enrolled women with locally advanced
cervical (18) or vaginal (2) cancer on chemoradiation; each received 50 mg
triapine as a 2-h IV infusion on day 1 and oral triapine 100 mg (n = 16) or
150 mg (n = 4) once daily, 5 days a week. NCT04234568 (NCI 10388, n = 16)
enrolled patients with gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours receiving
Lu-177 dotatate with oral triapine 100 mg (n = 3) or 150 mg (n = 13) once daily
on days 1-14. Twenty-four of the 36 patients were female; age ranged 23-74 years
and weight 41.8-138.4 kg. Six patients (all in NCI 9892) were active smokers.
The PK data were 573 quantifiable plasma concentrations (LLOQ 3 ug/L); the PD
data were 252 mHb observations from 33 patients.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Lee_2026_triapine")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: depot -> transit1 -> transit2 -> central (all at `ktr`), central <-> peripheral1, elimination from central | n/a | Results 'Population pharmacokinetic modeling', Figure 1, Methods S1 `@dynamics` |
| Oral bioavailability on the depot; IV doses into central | n/a | Methods S1 `@dosecontrol` (`bioav = (; Depot = _bioav)`) |
| `lktr` | log(3.11) 1/h | Table 2 Ktr |
| `lcl` | log(51.8) L/h | Table 2 CL (70 kg) |
| `lvc` | log(67.9) L | Table 2 Vc (70 kg) |
| `lq` | log(12.6) L/h | Table 2 Q (70 kg) |
| `lvp` | log(65.5) L | Table 2 Vp (70 kg) |
| `logitfdepot` | logit(0.76) | Table 2 F; logit-normal F, Methods 'Estimation methods' equation |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | Methods 'Covariate PK Model' allometric equation; Methods S1 `wtcl`, `wtv` |
| `e_smoke_cl` | 0.38 | Table 2 Effect_smoker; Results smoking equation `P = Ppop * (1 + beta * smoking status)` |
| `d/dt(effect) <- ke0 * (Cc - effect)` | n/a | Methods ke0 equation; Methods S2 `Ceff'` |
| `methb <- e0 * (1 + emax * effect^hill / (ec50^hill + effect^hill))` | n/a | Methods effect equation; Methods S2 `@vars` |
| `lke0` | log(0.36) 1/h | Table 2 ke0 |
| `le0` | log(0.95) % | Table 2 Ebase |
| `lemax` | log(100) (fixed) | Table 2 'Emax (fixed)'; Results PD paragraph |
| `lec50` | log(2535) ug/L | Table 2 EC50; Results PD paragraph (2535 ug/L) |
| `lhill` | log(1.63) | Table 2 Hill |
| `etalktr`, `etalcl`, `etalvc` | 0.2049, 0.0797, 0.0481 | Table 2 BSV 47.8, 28.8, 22.2 %CV; `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)` (Methods %CV formula) |
| `etalogitfdepot` | 2.283 | Table 2 BSV F 29.5 %CV, Methods delta-method formula, Methods S1 SD encoding (see Assumptions) |
| `etale0`, `etalec50` | 0.1137, 0.2891 | Table 2 BSV Ebase 34.7 %CV, EC50 57.9 %CV |
| `addSd`, `propSd` | 3.94 ug/L, 0.332 | Table 2 PK additive and proportional residual error |
| `addSd_methb`, `propSd_methb` | 0.13 %, 0.273 | Table 2 PD additive and proportional residual error |
| Combined error with summed variances (`combined2`) | n/a | Methods S1/S2 `Normal(f, sqrt(f^2 * sigma2_prop + sigma2_add))` |

# Typical-value checks

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Lee_2026_triapine")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Observation rows on the central state with dvid = 1: the model declares two
# endpoints (Cc and methb), and both come back as columns on every row.
obs_rows <- function(ids, times) {
  expand.grid(id = ids, time = times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
}
dose_rows <- function(ids, amt, route, time = 0) {
  data.frame(id = ids, time = time, amt = amt, evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_) |>
    mutate(
      cmt = if (route == "iv") "central" else "depot",
      # 2-h IV infusion (Methods); oral doses are boluses into the depot
      rate = if (route == "iv") amt / 2 else 0
    )
}

grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 8, by = 0.05), seq(8.5, 48, by = 0.5))))
ev_typ <- bind_rows(
  dose_rows(1, 50, "iv"), obs_rows(1, grid),
  dose_rows(2, 100, "po"), obs_rows(2, grid)
) |>
  mutate(WT = 70, SMOKE = 0) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

# One subject per solve: a typical-value (zeroRe) solve of several subjects
# at once warns that it has no omega.
typ <- bind_rows(lapply(split(ev_typ, ev_typ$id), function(d) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, d, returnType = "data.frame", useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
    mutate(id = d$id[1])
}))

typ_summary <- typ |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(
    tmax_Cc = time[which.max(Cc)],
    cmax_Cc = max(Cc),
    tmax_methb = time[which.max(methb)],
    max_methb = max(methb),
    methb_t0 = methb[time == 0],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(route = c("50 mg IV (2-h infusion)", "100 mg oral")[id])
knitr::kable(typ_summary |> select(route, everything(), -id), digits = 2)

# Closed-form exposure of a typical 70 kg nonsmoker: AUC0-inf = F * dose / CL.
auc_closed <- c(iv = 1000 * 50 / 51.8, po = 1000 * 0.76 * 100 / 51.8)
auc_trap <- typ |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(
    auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2) +
      Cc[n()] / (log(Cc[n() - 1] / Cc[n()]) / diff(tail(time, 2))),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
auc_check <- data.frame(
  route = c("IV 50 mg", "oral 100 mg"),
  auc_simulated = auc_trap$auc,
  auc_closed_form = unname(auc_closed)
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auc_simulated / auc_closed_form - 1))
knitr::kable(auc_check, digits = 2)

stopifnot(
  # The solve and its own closed form share every parameter, so the only
  # difference is integration / trapezoid error on a 0.05-h grid.
  all(abs(auc_check$pct_diff) < 1),
  # Baseline mHb before any drug is Ebase.
  all(abs(typ_summary$methb_t0 - 0.95) < 1e-6),
  # Figure S2: oral Cc peaks near 1.5 h and mHb near 3 h (counterclockwise hysteresis).
  typ_summary$tmax_Cc[2] >= 0.75, typ_summary$tmax_Cc[2] <= 2,
  typ_summary$tmax_methb[2] >= 2, typ_summary$tmax_methb[2] <= 4.5
)
```

For a typical 70 kg nonsmoker the model gives an oral 100 mg Cmax near
`r round(typ_summary$cmax_Cc[2])` ug/L at `r typ_summary$tmax_Cc[2]` h and a
methemoglobin peak of `r round(typ_summary$max_methb[2], 2)`% at
`r typ_summary$tmax_methb[2]` h, the delay that Figure S2 of the paper shows as a
counterclockwise hysteresis loop (median triapine peak at 1.5 h, median mHb peak
at 3 h).

```{r hysteresis, fig.cap = "Typical-value triapine concentration and methemoglobin after 100 mg oral (70 kg nonsmoker). Compare with Figure S2 of Lee 2026."}
typ |>
  filter(id == 2, time <= 12) |>
  ggplot(aes(Cc, methb)) +
  geom_path() +
  geom_point(data = function(d) filter(d, time %in% c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8))) +
  geom_text(
    data = function(d) filter(d, time %in% c(1, 1.5, 3, 6)),
    aes(label = paste0(time, " h")), nudge_y = 0.07, size = 3
  ) +
  labs(x = "Triapine Cc (ug/L)", y = "Methemoglobin (%)",
       title = "Concentration-effect hysteresis (typical subject)")
```

# Virtual cohort and NCA against Table S2

Table S2 of the paper reports the observed non-compartmental Cmax and
AUC0-inf (geometric means) per route, dose and smoking status. The virtual
cohort below has 200 subjects in each of the six route x dose x smoking cells.
Weights are drawn from a normal distribution with the NCI 9892 mean and SD
(77.4 +/- 14.1 kg), truncated to the pooled observed range (41.8-138.4 kg).

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260520)
set.seed(20260520)

arms <- expand.grid(
  regimen = c("Inf 50mg", "PO 100mg", "PO 150mg"),
  smoking = c("Nonsmoker", "Smoker"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
n_per_arm <- 200
nca_grid <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2, 2.25, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4,
              5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24)

make_arm <- function(i) {
  ids <- (i - 1) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  route <- if (arms$regimen[i] == "Inf 50mg") "iv" else "po"
  amt <- c("Inf 50mg" = 50, "PO 100mg" = 100, "PO 150mg" = 150)[[arms$regimen[i]]]
  wt <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_per_arm, 77.4, 14.1), 41.8), 138.4)
  bind_rows(dose_rows(ids, amt, route), obs_rows(ids, nca_grid)) |>
    left_join(data.frame(id = ids, WT = wt), by = "id") |>
    mutate(
      SMOKE = as.integer(arms$smoking[i] == "Smoker"),
      treatment = paste(arms$regimen[i], arms$smoking[i], sep = " | ")
    )
}
events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), make_arm)) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(length(unique(events$id)) == nrow(arms) * n_per_arm)

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, keep = "treatment",
                       returnType = "data.frame", useLinCmt = FALSE)
```

```{r vpc-cohort, fig.cap = "Simulated triapine Cc (median and 90% prediction interval, without residual error) by regimen and smoking status."}
sim |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), q50 = median(Cc), q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 3, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, ncol = 3) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Triapine Cc (ug/L)",
       caption = "Dotted line: LLOQ 3 ug/L.")
```

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, treatment, time)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  mutate(duration = ifelse(rate > 0, amt / rate, 0)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, duration, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, duration = "duration")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

```{r nca-compare}
# Table S2: observed geometric means (ug/L, ug*h/L)
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,              ~cmax, ~aucinf.obs,
  "Inf 50mg | Smoker",      262,   656,
  "Inf 50mg | Nonsmoker",   324,   903,
  "PO 100mg | Smoker",      286,   742,
  "PO 100mg | Nonsmoker",   544,  1321,
  "PO 150mg | Smoker",      252,  1067,
  "PO 150mg | Nonsmoker",   620,  1765
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/L", aucinf.obs = "ug*h/L", tmax = "h", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen | smoking" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Simulated (median) vs. observed (Table S2 geometric mean) NCA.",
    "* differs from the observed value by more than 20%."
  ))
```

```{r nca-assert}
sim_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(sim = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(published |> select(treatment, obs = aucinf.obs), by = "treatment") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim / obs - 1))
nonsmk <- filter(sim_auc, grepl("Nonsmoker", treatment))
stopifnot(
  # Nonsmoker arms (14-15 subjects each in Table S2): a mis-transcribed CL,
  # F or unit moves every arm by tens of percent.
  abs(median(nonsmk$pct_diff)) < 20,
  max(abs(nonsmk$pct_diff)) < 35
)
```

The nonsmoker arms, which hold 14-15 observed subjects each, agree with Table
S2 for AUC0-inf within about 15% and for Cmax within about 20%. The smoker arms
hold only 2-6 observed subjects each. The model's smoking effect (38% higher CL)
lowers the simulated AUC0-inf by about 28% relative to nonsmokers, whereas the
observed oral smoker geometric means are about 40-45% lower (Discussion), so the
simulated oral smoker AUC0-inf is about 30% above the observed values. The
smoking effect acts on CL only, so the model cannot reproduce the observed
halving of oral Cmax in smokers, notably in the two-subject 150 mg cell. The IV
smoker arm, where bioavailability plays no part, agrees within 5%.

# Replicate Figure 5a: single-dose dosing strategy

Figure 5a simulates a single oral dose of 100 mg in nonsmokers and 125 mg in
smokers, weights 40-100 kg, and reports the fraction of subjects with Cmax above
the 200 ug/L target and with peak mHb below the 10% threshold.

```{r fig5a-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(5)
set.seed(5)
n5 <- 200
grid5 <- c(seq(0, 6, by = 0.25), seq(7, 24, by = 1))
make_fig5 <- function(ids, amt, smoke, label) {
  bind_rows(dose_rows(ids, amt, "po"), obs_rows(ids, grid5)) |>
    left_join(data.frame(id = ids, WT = runif(length(ids), 40, 100)), by = "id") |>
    mutate(SMOKE = smoke, arm = label)
}
ev5 <- bind_rows(
  make_fig5(seq_len(n5), 100, 0, "Nonsmoker (100 mg)"),
  make_fig5(n5 + seq_len(n5), 125, 1, "Smoker (125 mg)")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim5 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev5, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame", useLinCmt = FALSE)
```

```{r fig5a, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5a of Lee 2026: median and 95% prediction interval (without residual error) of triapine Cc and methemoglobin after a single oral dose. Dashed lines: 200 ug/L target and 10% mHb threshold."}
sim5 |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  select(arm, time, Cc, methb) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, methb), names_to = "endpoint") |>
  group_by(arm, endpoint, time) |>
  summarise(q025 = quantile(value, 0.025), q50 = median(value),
            q975 = quantile(value, 0.975), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(endpoint = ifelse(endpoint == "Cc", "Triapine Cc (ug/L)", "Methemoglobin (%)")) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q025, ymax = q975), fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(colour = "blue") +
  geom_hline(
    data = data.frame(endpoint = c("Triapine Cc (ug/L)", "Methemoglobin (%)"),
                      y = c(200, 10)),
    aes(yintercept = y), linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  facet_grid(endpoint ~ arm, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = NULL)
```

```{r fig5a-table}
pct5 <- sim5 |>
  group_by(arm, id) |>
  summarise(cmax = max(Cc), mhb_max = max(methb), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    sim_cmax_above_200 = 100 * mean(cmax > 200),
    sim_mhb_below_10 = 100 * mean(mhb_max < 10),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    paper_cmax_above_200 = c(90.9, 93.9),
    paper_mhb_below_10 = c(92.4, 91.4)
  ) |>
  select(arm, sim_cmax_above_200, paper_cmax_above_200, sim_mhb_below_10, paper_mhb_below_10)
pct5 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm,
    "Cmax > 200 ug/L, simulated (%)" = sim_cmax_above_200,
    "Cmax > 200 ug/L, paper (%)" = paper_cmax_above_200,
    "Peak mHb < 10%, simulated (%)" = sim_mhb_below_10,
    "Peak mHb < 10%, paper (%)" = paper_mhb_below_10
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Target attainment, simulated (200 per arm) vs. Results text of Lee 2026.")

stopifnot(
  # 200 subjects per arm gives a Monte Carlo SE near 2 percentage points at
  # p = 0.9; a wrong F, CL, EC50 or Hill moves these by far more than 10.
  all(abs(pct5$sim_cmax_above_200 - pct5$paper_cmax_above_200) < 10),
  all(abs(pct5$sim_mhb_below_10 - pct5$paper_mhb_below_10) < 10)
)
```

# Replicate Figure 5b: between-occasion variability on bioavailability

Figure 5b simulates 100 mg oral triapine once daily for 28 days and adds an
"artificial" between-occasion variability (BOV, 0-60%) on bioavailability on top
of the BSV. The packaged model has no BOV, so it is added here as a
per-dose logit-scale shift `bovF`, by piping a replacement `fdepot` line into the
model. The BOV percentage is converted to a logit-scale SD with the same delta
method the paper uses for the F %CV, SD = BOV / (1 - Fpop). Exceedance is counted
on the predicted mHb with the PD residual error added, per dosing interval (a
"dose") and per subject (any interval).

```{r fig5b}
mod_bov <- mod |> rxode2::model(fdepot <- expit(logitfdepot + etalogitfdepot + bovF))
rxode2::rxSetSeed(28)
set.seed(28)
n_bov <- 200
dose_times <- 24 * (0:27)
obs_after <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12)
bov_levels <- c(0, 20, 40, 60)

bov_events <- function(level, offset) {
  ids <- offset + seq_len(n_bov)
  occ <- expand.grid(id = ids, occ = seq_along(dose_times)) |>
    mutate(bovF = rnorm(n(), 0, (level / 100) / (1 - 0.76)))
  doses <- expand.grid(id = ids, occ = seq_along(dose_times)) |>
    mutate(time = dose_times[occ], amt = 100, rate = 0, evid = 1L,
           cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, occ = seq_along(dose_times), dt = obs_after) |>
    mutate(time = dose_times[occ] + dt, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L,
           cmt = "central", dvid = 1L) |>
    select(-dt)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    left_join(occ, by = c("id", "occ")) |>
    left_join(data.frame(id = ids, WT = runif(n_bov, 40, 100)), by = "id") |>
    mutate(SMOKE = 0, bov = level) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
ev_bov <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(bov_levels), function(i) {
  bov_events(bov_levels[i], (i - 1) * n_bov)
}))
sim_bov <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_bov, ev_bov, keep = c("bov", "occ"),
                           returnType = "data.frame", useLinCmt = FALSE)

ini_df <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$iniDf
add_methb <- ini_df$est[ini_df$name == "addSd_methb"]
prop_methb <- ini_df$est[ini_df$name == "propSd_methb"]
sim_bov <- sim_bov |>
  mutate(methb_obs = methb + rnorm(n()) * sqrt(add_methb^2 + (prop_methb * methb)^2))

by_dose <- sim_bov |>
  group_by(bov, id, occ) |>
  summarise(exceed = any(methb_obs > 10), exceed_pred = any(methb > 10), .groups = "drop")
fig5b <- by_dose |>
  group_by(bov) |>
  summarise(
    dose_pct = 100 * mean(exceed),
    subject_pct = 100 * mean(tapply(exceed, id, any)),
    dose_pct_no_ruv = 100 * mean(exceed_pred),
    subject_pct_no_ruv = 100 * mean(tapply(exceed_pred, id, any)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(paper_dose_pct = c(4.6, 5.6, 5.9, 6.2), paper_subject_pct = c(10.3, 10.9, 12.6, 13.7))

fig5b |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "BOV (%)" = bov,
    "Doses > 10% mHb, simulated" = dose_pct,
    "Doses, paper" = paper_dose_pct,
    "Subjects > 10% mHb, simulated" = subject_pct,
    "Subjects, paper" = paper_subject_pct,
    "Doses, no residual error" = dose_pct_no_ruv,
    "Subjects, no residual error" = subject_pct_no_ruv
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Replicates Figure 5b of Lee 2026 (200 simulated nonsmokers per BOV level; percentages).")

stopifnot(
  # Dose-level exceedance stays in the single digits at every BOV level, as in
  # the paper; the subject-level fraction depends on draws in the tails, so it
  # is reported, not asserted.
  all(fig5b$dose_pct < 15)
)
```

Without residual error and without BOV, every dose of a subject gives the
same peak, so the dose- and subject-level fractions coincide (about 5-6%,
close to the paper's dose-level 4.6%). The paper's subject-level 10.3% at 0%
BOV is about twice its dose-level value, which implies per-dose randomness in
its exceedance count, most likely residual error; with the PD residual error
added here, both fractions are a few points above the paper's. In both
versions the subject-level fraction rises with BOV while the dose-level
fraction changes little, the pattern Figure 5b reports. The paper does not
state the weight distribution, smoking status or sampling times of this
simulation, and with 200 subjects per level the subject-level percentages
carry a Monte Carlo SE of about 2-3 percentage points.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Variance of the logit-normal bioavailability.** Table 2 gives only the %CV
  of F (29.5%), computed with the delta method `(1 - Fpop) * sqrt(omega^2)`
  (Methods), which gives `omega^2 = (0.295 / 0.24)^2 = 1.511`. The Methods
  equation writes `etaF ~ Normal(logit(Fpop), omega^2)`, but the authors' Pumas
  code (Methods S1) passes that parameter, `Omega2_bio`, as the second argument
  of `Normal()`, which in Julia is the standard deviation (the other random
  effects in the same code are written `Normal(0, sqrt(Omega2))`). The code is
  what was fitted, so the packaged model uses a logit-scale SD of 1.511
  (`etalogitfdepot ~ 2.283`). Reading the equation literally instead
  (`etalogitfdepot ~ 1.511`) gives 92-94% of subjects above the Cmax target in
  the Figure 5a check instead of 88-90%, slightly closer to the 90.9% / 93.9%
  the paper reports; users who prefer that reading can set
  `ini(etalogitfdepot = 1.511)`.
- **PD random effects follow Table 2, not Methods S2.** The PD code in
  Methods S2 fixes EC50 at 900 and estimates Emax with a random effect, while
  Table 2 and the Results text report the final PD model with Emax fixed at
  100, EC50 estimated (2535 ug/L) and BSV on Ebase and EC50. The supplied code
  is an earlier iteration of the PD model; the packaged model follows the final
  estimates in Table 2.
- **Transit rate constant.** The Results text says Ktr "was estimated to be
  1.0/h", but Table 2 reports 3.11 1/h (bootstrap 95% CI 2.63-3.72) and Table
  S1 3.16 / 2.94 1/h; the Table 2 value is used.
- **Units printed in Table 2.** EC50 is printed with unit mg/L but the Results
  text gives 2535 ug/L, the unit of the plasma concentrations (LLOQ 3 ug/L);
  ug/L is used. The PD additive residual error is printed in ug/L but applies to
  mHb in %; it is 0.13 percentage points.
- **Emax is a fold increase over baseline.** In the paper's effect equation
  `E = Ebase * (1 + Emax * Ceff^h / (EC50^h + Ceff^h))`, Emax = 100 multiplies
  Ebase, so the model's ceiling is 0.95 x 101 = 96% methemoglobin; Table 2
  lists its unit as %.
- **Sequential fit.** The paper fitted PD to the individual PK predictions;
  the packaged model simulates PK and PD jointly. No covariance between PK and
  PD random effects was reported, and none is assumed.
- **Residual error.** Both endpoints use the combined error with summed
  variances (`combined2()`), matching the Pumas `Normal(f, sqrt(f^2 *
  sigma2_prop + sigma2_add))`. Table 2 reports the SDs (the Laplace variances
  in Table S1, 14.8 ug^2/L^2 and 0.10, are the squares of values near 3.9 ug/L
  and 0.32).
- **Smoking indicator.** `SMOKE` = 1 for an active smoker, 0 otherwise, as in
  the paper's binary smoking-status covariate; former smokers were not
  distinguished.
- **Virtual cohorts.** Weights for the NCA cohort are drawn from a truncated
  normal (77.4 +/- 14.1 kg, 41.8-138.4 kg); the Figure 5 cohorts use a uniform
  40-100 kg distribution, matching the range the paper states. Figure 5b
  subjects are nonsmokers.
- No erratum or correction notice for this article was found as of
  2026-11-13.
